FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the 
draft finalized by the Dyes Intermediates Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 


N,N-Bis-hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine (C11Hi7NO2) is an important intermediate used in the 
manufacture of azodispersedyes. It has the following structural formula. 


OH 


OH 
H3C 


N,N-BIS-HYDROXYETHYL-META-TOLUIDINE 
[Molecular Mass: 195.0] 
(CAS Registry No. 91-99-6) 


This standard was first published in 2001. Considering the development in latest analytical 
techniques, the Committee decided to revise this standard. In this (first) revision method for GLC 
method has been included for determination of assay and impurities. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex 
C. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular reguirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded 
off in accordance with IS 2 : 2022 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision). 
'The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of 
the specified value in this standard. 


IS 15082 : 2022 


Indian Standard 
N,N-BIS-HYDROXYETHYL-META-TOLUIDINE, TECHNICAL — 
SPECIFICATION 
(First Revision) 
1 SCOPE IS No Title 


This standard prescribes the requirements, 
the methods of sampling and testing for 
N,N-bis-hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions, 
which through reference in this text, 
constitute the provisions of this standard. At 
the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revisions and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of 
applying the most recent editions of the 
standards indicated below: 


1070: 1992 Reagent grade water — 
Specification (third revision) 


2552: 1989 Steel drums (galvanized and 
ungalvanized) — 
Specification (third revision) 


5299 : 2001 Methods of sampling and 
tests fordye intermediates 
(first revision) 


3 REQUIREMENTS 
3.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of off 
white solid material. 


3.2 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1, when tested 
according to the methods prescribed in col 4 
and col 5 of Table 1.

4 PACKING AND MARKING 
4.1 Packing 


The material shall be packed in steel drums 
(conforming to 1S 2552) lined with suitable 
polyethylene film or as agreed to between 
the purchaser and the supplier. Each 
container shall be securely closed. 


4.2 Marking 


4.2.1 Each container shall bear legibly and 
indelibly the following information: 


a) Name of the material; 


b) Name of manufacturer and his 
recognized trade-mark, if any; 


c) Net mass of material; 

d) Month and year of the manufacture; 

e) Batch or lot number; and 

f) Any other statutory requirements. 
4.2.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the 
requirements of this standard may be 
certified as per the conformity assessment 
schemes under the provisions of the Bureau 
of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 


products may be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


5 SAMPLING 


5.1 The method of drawing representative 
samples of the material shall be as 
prescribed in 4 of IS 5299. 


5.2 Number of Tests 


5.2.1 Tests for the determination of N,N-bis- 
hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine (assay), N- 
hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine and meta- 
toluidine content, shall be conducted on the 
individual samples. 


5.2.2 Tests for the determination of 
remaining characteristics, namely, 
description, crystallizing temperature, 
moisture content and insoluble in dilute HCl 
shall be conducted on the composite sample. 


5.3 Criteria for Conformity 
5.3.1 For Individual Samples 


The lot shall be declared as conforming to 
the requirement of N,N-bis-hydroxyethyl- 
meta-toluidine (assay), N-hydroxyethyl- 
meta-toluidine and meta-toluidine content, if 
each of the individual test results satisfies 
the relevant requirements given in Table 1. 


5.3.2 For Composite Sample 


For declaring the conformity of the lot to the 
requirements of all other characteristics 
(5.2.2) tested on the composite sample, the 
test results for each of the characteristics 
shall satisfy the relevant requirements given 
in 3. 


6 TEST METHODS 


6.1 Tests shall be conducted according to the 
methods prescribed and as referred in col 4 
and col 5 of Table 1. 


IS 15082 : 2022 


6.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals 
and distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be 
employed in tests. 


NOTE — "Pure chemicals' shall mean 
chemicals that donot contain impurities 
which affect the results of analysis. 


IS 15082 : 2022 


ANNEX A 
[Table 1, SI No. (ii), (111) and (iv)] 


DETERMINATION OF N, N-BIS-HYDROXYETHYL-META-TOLUIDINE CONTENT 
AND ITS IMPURITIES 


A-1 GENERAL 


Two methods namely method A, Titration 
Method (A-2) and method B, Gas Liquid 
Chromatography (GLC) (A-3) have been 
prescribed for the determination of N,N-bis- 
hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine and its 
impurities. Any of these two methods can be 
used on routine basis. However, in the case 
of disputes, Gas Liquid Chromatography 
(GLC) method (A-3) shall be the referee 
method. 


A-2 METHOD A 
A-2.1 Summary of the Method 


A diazonium solution is prepared by 
reacting 2,4-dinitroaniline in concentrated 
sulphuric acid with sodium nitrite solution. 
It is standardized by titrating against N,N- 
bis-hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine of known 
purity. The sample of N,N-bis- 
hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine is then titrated 
against this standard diazonium solution. 


A-2.2 Reagents 
A-2.2.1 Glacial acetic acid 


A-2.2.2 Concentrated sulphuric acid, 98 
percent (m/v). 


A-2.2.3 Dilute acetic acid, 20 percent (m/v). 


A-2.2.4 Sodium acetate solution, 20 percent 
(m/v). 


A-2.2.5 H-acid indicator solution 


Dissolve 0.5 g of H-acid in 100 ml of water 
containing 1 g of soda ash. 


A-2.2.6 2,4-Dinitroaniline, 99 percent pure. 


A-2.2.7 N,N-Bis-hydroxyethyl-meta- 
toluidine, reference sample of known purity. 


A-2.3 Procedure 


A-2.3.1 Preparation of 2,4-dinitroaniline 
diazo solution 


Take 600 g (326 ml) of concentrated 
sulphuric acid (98 percent) in a reaction 
vesselwith stirrer which is cooled to 10°C 
externally on icebath. Add 69 g of sodium 
nitrite (100 percent) gradually under stirring 
maintaining the temperature below 10°C. 
After the addition is complete, remove the 
ice bath and bring it to room temperature 
and then raise to 60°C to dissolve the 
material completely. After the dissolution is 
complete the temperature is again brought 
below 20°C. Similarly, prepare a slurry of 
2,4-dinitroaniline in sulphuric acid by 
dissolving 183 g of 2,4-dinitroaniline in 200 
g of sulphuric acid in a 500 ml beaker. Add 
this slurry to the nitrosulphuric acid slurry 
prepared earlier maintaining the temperature 
below 20°C. After the addition is complete, 
stir for another 2 h for the completion of 
reaction (stock solution). Depending upon 
the requirements, a portion of this slurry is 
taken out and diluted with 10 times by its 
volume with ice water (for example, 10 ml 
of stock solution and 90 ml of icewater). 
The solution is then clarified with activated 
carbon and filtered before use. It is to be 
noted that the diluted diazo solution is not 
stable and hence should be prepared fresh 
every time before use. 


A-2.3.2 Standardization of 2,4- 
dinitroaniline diazonium solution 


Weigh exactly 0.780 9 g of N,N-bis- 
hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine (99 percent) 
and transfer it to a 1 1 beaker. Dissolve it 
with 10-15 ml of glacial acetic acid and 
dilute the solution with ice water to 500 ml. 
Add about 10 ml of 20 percent sodium 
acetate solution (m/v) to bring the pH 
between 4 to 6. Titrate this solution with 
2,4-dinitroaniline diazo (diluted) until the 
solution shows the presence of an excess 
diazo with H-acid (bluish black coloration). 
This is checked by taking a drop of the 
reaction mixture and a drop of a diluted 
solution of H-acid on a piece of filter paper. 
The bluish black coloration in the junction 
of the two liquids indicates that the end 
point is reached. Throughout the titration, 
the pH should be maintained between 4 to 6. 


A-2.3.3 Repeat the titration as prescribed in 
A-2.3.2, using the test sample of N,N-bis- 
hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine. 


A-2.4 Calculation 


A-2.4.1 Normalityofdiazonium salt, 


Px0.780 
EE 


where 


P = purity (percent by mass) of the 
known sample; and 


V = volume of diazonium solution 
required for the known sample, ml. 


A-2.4.2 Assay, percent by mass = 
V XN x 19.5 
0.780 


where 


Vı = volume of diazonium solution 
required for the test sample, ml; 
and 


IS 15082 : 2022 


N = normality of diazonium solution 
A-3 METHOD B 
A-3.1 General 


The contents of N,N-bis-hydroxyethyl-meta- 
toluidine and possible impurities, namely 
meta-toluidine and N-hydroxyethyl-meta- 
toluidine are determined by gas liquid 
chromatographic method (GLC). 


A-3.2 Apparatus 
A-3.2.1 Gas chromatograph 


Any gas chromatograph equipped with a 
flame ionized detector (FID), a split/splitless 
injector and a suitable electronic 
integrator/software can be used with 
following accessories and operating 
condition: 


A-3.2.1.1 Capillary column of length 15 m; 
internal diameter 0.53 mm and film 
thickness 1.5 um or equivalent column. 


A-3.2.1.2 Injector, with temperature: 260 
°C; split ratio: 10 and carrier gas: nitrogen 
or helium with flow control mode pressure. 


A-3.2.1.3 Oven temperature programming 


Heating Rate Temperature Hold Time 
(°C/min) (°C) (min) 
— 100 0 

10 290 10 
A-3.2.1.4 FID parameters 
Hydrogen Flow: 40 ml/min 
Air Flow: 400 ml/min 
Temperature: 290°C 


NOTE — The above gas chromatographic 
(GC) conditions are suggestive. However, 


IS 15082 : 2022 


any GC method having difference in 
detector, column packing material and type 
(like packed/capillary, diameter, length, film 
thickness etc), calibration technique 
(internal standard, external standard, area 
normalization, percent area etc), carrier gas 
(He, H2, N2) may be used with applicable 
GC operating parameters, provided 
standardization and calibration of the 
components is established after setting GC 
parameters for the resolution and accuracy 
level as specified in this standard. 


A-3.3 Reagent 
A-3.3.1 Acetone, AR grade. 


A-3.3.2 N,N-bis-hydroxyethyl-meta- 
toluidine, technical. 


A-3.3.3 m-Toluidine. 
A-3.4 Standard Preparation 


Weight accurately 1 g of standard N,N-bis- 
hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine in 100 ml 
volumetric flask dissolve in acetone and 
make the volume up to the mark with 
acetone. 


A-3.5 Sample Preparation 


Weight accurately 1 g of sample in 100 ml 
volumetric flask. Dissolve it in acetone and 
make the volume up to the mark with 
acetone. 


A-3.6 Injection volume, 1.0 ul. 


A-3.7 Retention Time 


meta-Toluidine: 4.21 min 
N-Hydroxyethyl-m-toluidine: 9.38 min 


N,N-Bis-hydroxyethyl-meta- 


toluidine: 13.21 min 


A-3.8 Calculation 


Calculate the peak area of individual 
constituent pertaining to N,N-bis- 
hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine on the 
chromatogram of the material. The 
concentration of the constituent may be 
obtained on the basis of peak area on 
chromatogram obtained with standard N,N- 
bishydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine. 


N,N-Bishydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine, 


percent = ——————— x 100 
Ay SH: xW3 x B4 


where 


Aı = area of standard N,N- 
bishydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine; 


Vı = injection volume of standard 
N,N-bishydroxyethyl-meta- 
toluidine; 


Wı = weight of standard N,N- 
bishydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine; 


Bi = total volume of standard N,N- 
bishydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine; 


A2 = area of N,N-bishydroxyethyl- 
meta-toluidine peak in sample; 


V2 = injection volume of sample; 
Wo = weight of sample; and 


B2 = total volume of sample.

ANNEX B 
[Table 1, SI No. (iii) and (iv)] 


DETERMINATION OF N-HYDROXYETHYL-META-TOLUIDINE AND META- 
TOLUIDIENE BY THIN LAYER CHROMATOGRAPHY 


B-1 GENERAL 


The impurities, namely, N-hydroxyethyl- 
meta-toluidine and meta-toluidine can be 
determined by thin layer chromatography 
(TLC) as well as by gas liquid 
chromatography (GLC) method as given 
under A-3. In case of dispute Gas Liquid 
Chromatography method (A-3) shall be 
considered as referee method. 


B-2 APPARATUS 


B-2.1 Thin Layer Chromatographic 
Chamber, 25 cm x 25 cm. 


B-2.2 Micropipette, 10 ul capacity. 


B-2.3 Thin Layer Chromatography 
Plates, size 20 cm x 20 cm. 


B-2.4 Nitrous Fumes Chamber 


A glass chamber of size 25 cm x 25 cm with 
a beaker of capacity 100 ml containing 
approximately 50 ml of concentrated 
hydrochloric acid (HCI) [30 percent,(m/v)]. 
The nitrous fumes are generated by adding a 
little solid sodium nitrite every time before 
inserting the plate. 


B-3 REAGENTS 


B-3.1 N-hydroxyethyl-meta-toluidine and 
Meta-toluidine, Pure (reference samples) 


Prepare 0.001 percent, 0.002 percent, 0.004 
percent solutions in methanol. 


B-3.2 Eluent Ethyl Acetate: Toluene, 
80:20 (vw). 


B-3.3 Spray Reagent, about 1 percent 
solution of para nitro aniline diazo. 


B-4 PROCEDURE 


Weigh 2 g of the sample under test (100 
percent) basis and dissolve in 100 ml 
methanol. Take a plate coated with silica gel 
G and spot 10 ul of each of the test solution 
and reference solution along the start line at 
a distance of 3 cm from one another. 
Saturate the chromatographic chamber with 
the eluent. Insert the plate in the chamber 
and allow to run for about 60 min during 
which time the solvent front travels 
approximately 10 cm past the start line. 
Remove the plate from the chamber dry it in 
air. After drying spray, the plate with para- 
nitroaniline diazo solution when the spots 
(reddish orange) characteristic of meta- 
toluidine and N-hydroxyethyl-meta- 
toluidine become visible at Ry (retardation 
factor) values of 0.90 and 0.70 respectively. 


B-5 Reporting 


Estimate the quantities of the impurities by 
comparing the colour intensity of the spots 
of the material under test with those of the 
solutions of the reference samples. 


IS 15082 : 2022
